title: Soil Erosion Risk Analysis for Semi-Arid Regions
text: aridRUSLE R package implementing modified RUSLE (Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation) approach soil erosion risk analysis semi-arid arid regions worldwide. Rather requiring five classical RUSLE factors, package focuses three key factors derivable easily accessible remote sensing climate datasets: rainfall erosivity (R), topographic influence (LS), vegetation cover (C). Soil erodibility (K) conservation practices (P) deliberately omitted due typical data limitations semi-arid research areas. ensure accurate C-factor estimation, package includes dedicated water masking step. Open water surfaces produce misleading NDVI values otherwise bias vegetation cover factor — applying apply_water_mask() calc_c_factor() removes pixels prevents propagating final erosion risk index. aridRUSLE designed global applicability across semi-arid arid climate regimes. R-factor module supports five different empirical formulas, calibrated distinct regional climate. appropriate formula automatically selected based geographic coordinates study area using Köppen-like climate zone classification, can set manually. makes package readily applicable across Mediterranean, Sahel, Arabian Peninsula, Central Asia, Australia, South America without manual formula lookup. ## Dependencies aridRUSLE requires following R packages, installed automatically: terra, ggplot2, tidyterra, ggspatial, kgc

what: Water mask to mask out lakes
title: Soil Erosion Risk Analysis for Semi-Arid Regions
text: apply_water_mask() computes Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) internally multi-band satellite image uses mask open water pixels target raster NDVI composite. required preprocessing step calc_c_factor(), water surfaces produce misleading NDVI values. Optionally, smoothing filter minimum patch size threshold can applied remove isolated artefacts retain true water bodies.
code: sentinel  <- terra::rast("sentinel2.tif") ndvi      <- terra::rast("ndvi.tif")  ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(                  target_raster   = ndvi,                  satelite_raster = sentinel,                  green_band      = 3,                         nir_band        = 8,                         threshold       = 0.3,                       smooth          = TRUE,                      smooth_w        = 3,                         min_water_ha    = 1,                         return_ndwi     = FALSE,                  plot            = TRUE                )

title: Soil Erosion Risk Analysis for Semi-Arid Regions
text: calc_r_factor() computes RUSLE rainfall erosivity (R-factor) precipitation raster using empirical formula automatically selected climate zone study area. climate zone detected geographic coordinates via Köppen-Geiger classification, can set manually. Five formulas supported, calibrated different semi-arid arid climate regime.
code: precip <- terra::rast("chirps_seasonal.tif")  r_factor <- calc_r_factor(               precip_raster = precip,               lat           = -30.5,                      lon           = -70.2,                      climate_zone  = NULL,                       season_days   = 243,                        a             = 0.171,                      b             = 1.212,                      verbose       = TRUE,               plot          = TRUE             )

what: Calculation of topographic influence on erosion (LS-factor)
title: Soil Erosion Risk Analysis for Semi-Arid Regions
text: calc_ls_factor() computes RUSLE topographic LS-factor digital elevation model (DEM) using Moore & Burch (1986) approach. factor combines slope length slope steepness single dimensionless value representing topographic influence soil erosion. DEM provided geographic CRS (WGS84), automatically reprojected appropriate UTM zone computation.
code: dem <- terra::rast("srtm.tif")  ls_factor <- calc_ls_factor(                dem     = dem,                verbose = TRUE,                plot    = TRUE              )

what: Calculation of vegetation cover influence of erosion (C-factor)
title: Soil Erosion Risk Analysis for Semi-Arid Regions
text: calc_c_factor() computes RUSLE vegetation cover factor (C-factor) water-masked NDVI composite using exponential relationship Mahgoub et al. (2012). C-factor ranges 0 (dense vegetation, erosion) 1 (bare soil, maximum erosion). strongly recommended apply apply_water_mask() NDVI composite passing function.
code: ndvi <- terra::rast("ndvi.tif")  # Step 1: mask water pixels first ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(target_raster   = ndvi,                                 satelite_raster = sentinel)  # Step 2: compute C-factor from masked NDVI c_factor <- calc_c_factor(               ndvi_raster = ndvi_masked,               verbose     = TRUE,               plot        = TRUE             )

title: Soil Erosion Risk Analysis for Semi-Arid Regions
text: calc_erosion_risk() combines R, LS, C factors dimensionless Erosion Risk Index (ERI) normalising factor 0–1 multiplying pixel-wise. input rasters share geometry, automatically reprojected resampled match LS-factor grid. result displayed publication-quality cartographic map north arrow, scale bar, coordinate grid.
code: result <- calc_erosion_risk(             r_factor        = r_factor,             ls_factor       = ls_factor,             c_factor        = c_factor,             normalize       = TRUE,             resample_method = "bilinear",             plot            = TRUE,             map_title       = "Soil Erosivity",             figure_caption  = NULL,             data_source     = "NASA JPL (2023). SRTM Global 1 arc second (30m)"           )

what: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
title: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
text: Masks water pixels target raster (typically NDVI composite) based NDWI values computed internally multi-band satelite image. Required preprocessing step calc_c_factor(), open water surfaces produce misleading NDVI values.

title: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
code: apply_water_mask(   target_raster,   satelite_raster,   green_band = 3,   nir_band = 8,   threshold = 0.3,   smooth = TRUE,   smooth_w = 3,   min_water_ha = 1,   return_ndwi = FALSE,   plot = TRUE )

title: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
text: target_raster SpatRaster. raster masked (e.g. NDVI composite). layers masked simultaneously. satelite_raster SpatRaster. Multi-band satelite image containing least green NIR bands. Used compute NDWI internally. green_band Integer. Band index green band satelite_raster. Default: 3 (Sentinel-2 Band 3). Use 3 standard Sentinel-2 multiband images. Adjust using False Colour Composite different sensor. nir_band Integer. Band index NIR band satelite_raster. Default: 8 (Sentinel-2 Band 8). Use 1 working Sentinel-2 False Colour Composite (RGB = NIR / Red / Green). threshold Numeric. NDWI threshold pixels classified water set NA output. Default: 0.3 (McFeeters 1996). smooth Logical. TRUE, applies mean filter NDWI raster thresholding reduce isolated resampling artefacts water-land boundaries. Window size controlled smooth_w. Default: TRUE. smooth_w Integer. Window size smoothing filter (must odd integer >= 3). used smooth = TRUE. Default: 3. min_water_ha Numeric NULL. Minimum area hectares connected water patch masked. Patches smaller threshold kept land. Converted pixels automatically based resolution satelite_raster. NULL, pixels threshold masked regardless patch size. Recommended: 1 (FAO standard) semi-arid regions. return_ndwi Logical. TRUE, internally computed NDWI raster (smoothing, applicable) stored attribute (attr(result, "ndwi")) returned object. Default: FALSE. plot Logical. TRUE (default), displays masked raster (first layer) water pixels shown steelblue. Useful visually inspecting mask adjusting threshold min_water_ha needed.

title: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
text: SpatRaster dimensions CRS target_raster. Water pixels set NA, pixels unchanged. return_ndwi = TRUE, computed NDWI raster accessible via attr(result, "ndwi").

title: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
text: NDWI calculated : $$NDWI = \frac{Green - NIR}{Green + NIR}$$ Band indices default standard Sentinel-2 band numbering (green_band = 3, nir_band = 8). Adjust using different sensor band ordering (e.g. False Colour Composite NIR stored band 1). target_raster satelite_raster share geometry (extent, resolution, CRS), satelite_raster automatically resampled match target_raster using nearest-neighbour interpolation masking. smooth = TRUE, NDWI raster spatially smoothed mean filter thresholding. reduces isolated salt--pepper pixels caused resampling artefacts water-land boundaries. min_water_ha set, connected water patches area least min_water_ha hectares masked. removes isolated single pixels small artefacts, retaining true water bodies lakes reservoirs. minimum area converted pixels automatically based resolution satelite_raster, making threshold resolution-independent scientifically justifiable. Recommended values based literature: 0.1 ha — EU Water Framework Directive minimum mapping unit 1.0 ha — FAO Irrigation & Drainage standard 4.0 ha — typical Landsat-based (30 m) studies Setting plot = TRUE displays masked result user can visually inspect water mask adjust threshold min_water_ha needed proceeding calc_c_factor().

title: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
text: McFeeters, S.K. (1996). use Normalised Difference Water Index (NDWI) delineation open water features. International Journal Remote Sensing, 17(7), 1425-1432.

title: Mask water pixels using an NDWI threshold — apply_water_mask
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ndvi <- terra::rast("s2_ndvi.tif") s2   <- terra::rast("s2_bands.tif")  # standard multi-band Sentinel-2 image  # Mask water pixels with default settings (Sentinel-2 bands, smooth = TRUE) ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(ndvi, s2)  # Only mask water bodies >= 1 ha (FAO standard) ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(ndvi, s2, min_water_ha = 1)  # False Colour Composite (NIR stored as band 1) s2_fcc      <- terra::rast("sentinel_false_colour.tif") ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(ndvi, s2_fcc, green_band = 3, nir_band = 1,                                 min_water_ha = 1)  # Inspect the result visually before proceeding ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(ndvi, s2, min_water_ha = 1, plot = TRUE)  # Disable smoothing and patch filtering ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(ndvi, s2, smooth = FALSE,                                 min_water_ha = NULL)  # Retrieve the internally computed NDWI raster ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(ndvi, s2, return_ndwi = TRUE) ndwi        <- attr(ndvi_masked, "ndwi") } # }

title: Calculate Vegetation Cover Factor (C-Factor) — calc_c_factor
text: Computes RUSLE C-factor (vegetation cover management factor) water-masked NDVI composite using exponential relationship proposed Mahgoub et al. (2012). C-factor ranges 0 (dense vegetation, erosion) 1 (bare soil, maximum erosion).

title: Calculate Vegetation Cover Factor (C-Factor) — calc_c_factor
code: calc_c_factor(ndvi_raster, verbose = TRUE, plot = TRUE)

title: Calculate Vegetation Cover Factor (C-Factor) — calc_c_factor
text: ndvi_raster SpatRaster. NDVI composite values range -1 1. water-masked beforehand using apply_water_mask(). Water pixels (NA) preserved NA output. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints summary computed C-factor (min, mean, max) console. Default: TRUE. plot Logical. TRUE, displays map C-factor computation. Default: TRUE.

title: Calculate Vegetation Cover Factor (C-Factor) — calc_c_factor
text: SpatRaster one layer C-factor values range 0 1 (dimensionless), extent, resolution CRS ndvi_raster. Water pixels NA. layer named "C_factor".

title: Calculate Vegetation Cover Factor (C-Factor) — calc_c_factor
text: C-factor calculated : $$C = 0.353 \cdot e^{1.669 \cdot NDVI}$$ Output values clamped range 0 1. Water pixels (NA input) remain NA output propagate automatically final erosion risk index computed calc_erosion_risk(). strongly recommended apply apply_water_mask() NDVI composite passing function, open water surfaces produce misleading NDVI values otherwise bias C-factor.

title: Calculate Vegetation Cover Factor (C-Factor) — calc_c_factor
text: Mahgoub, M. et al. (2012). Estimation soil loss semi-arid area using RUSLE model remote sensing. CATENA, 100, 126-133.

title: Calculate Vegetation Cover Factor (C-Factor) — calc_c_factor
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   ndvi <- terra::rast("s2_ndvi.tif")   s2   <- terra::rast("s2_bands.tif")    # Step 1: mask water pixels   ndvi_masked <- apply_water_mask(ndvi, s2)    # Step 2: compute C-factor from masked NDVI   c_factor <- calc_c_factor(ndvi_masked)    # Without plot   c_factor <- calc_c_factor(ndvi_masked, plot = FALSE) } # }

what: Combine factors into an Erosion Risk Index (ERI) — calc_erosion_risk
title: Combine factors into an Erosion Risk Index (ERI) — calc_erosion_risk
text: Normalises R, LS C 0-1 multiplies pixel-wise produce Erosion Risk Index (ERI). rasters share geometry (extent, resolution, CRS), automatically reprojected resampled match ls_factor (used reference grid).

title: Combine factors into an Erosion Risk Index (ERI) — calc_erosion_risk
code: calc_erosion_risk(   r_factor,   ls_factor,   c_factor,   normalize = TRUE,   resample_method = "bilinear",   plot = TRUE,   map_title = "Soil Erosivity",   figure_caption = NULL,   data_source = NULL )

title: Combine factors into an Erosion Risk Index (ERI) — calc_erosion_risk
text: r_factor SpatRaster. Output calc_r_factor(). ls_factor SpatRaster. Output calc_ls_factor(). Used reference grid alignment. c_factor SpatRaster. Output calc_c_factor(). normalize Logical. TRUE (default), factor min-max normalised 0-1 multiplication. resample_method Character. Resampling method passed terra::resample(). Default: "bilinear". plot Logical. TRUE (default), displays publication-style map ERI. map_title Character. Title printed map. Default: "Soil Erosivity". figure_caption Character. Figure caption printed map plot subtitle. Default: NULL (caption). data_source Character. Data-source string printed map small type. Default: NULL (source line).

title: Combine factors into an Erosion Risk Index (ERI) — calc_erosion_risk
text: Invisibly returns list two elements: eri SpatRaster (0-1) Erosion Risk Index values, named "ERI". map ggplot object, NULL plot = FALSE.

title: Combine factors into an Erosion Risk Index (ERI) — calc_erosion_risk
text: ERI calculated : $$ERI = R_{norm} \times LS_{norm} \times C_{norm}$$ factor min-max normalised \([0, 1]\) multiplication. Higher ERI values indicate greater erosion hazard. plot = TRUE, ERI displayed publication-quality cartographic layout built ggplot2, tidyterra ggspatial: cream--brown colour ramp, coordinate grid degree labels, north arrow, scale bar, continuous legend, optional title, figure caption data source line.

title: Combine factors into an Erosion Risk Index (ERI) — calc_erosion_risk
text: Mahgoub, M. et al. (2012). Estimation soil loss semi-arid area using RUSLE model remote sensing. CATENA, 100, 126-133.

title: Calculate Topographic LS-Factor — calc_ls_factor
text: Computes RUSLE LS-factor (slope length x slope steepness) digital elevation model (DEM) using Moore & Burch (1986) approach.

title: Calculate Topographic LS-Factor — calc_ls_factor
code: calc_ls_factor(dem, verbose = TRUE, plot = TRUE)

title: Calculate Topographic LS-Factor — calc_ls_factor
text: dem SpatRaster. Digital elevation model elevation values metres. geographic CRS (degrees), automatically reprojected appropriate UTM zone. missing CRS trigger error. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints summary computed LS-factor (min, mean, max) cell size used console. Default: TRUE. plot Logical. TRUE, displays map LS-factor computation. Default: TRUE.

title: Calculate Topographic LS-Factor — calc_ls_factor
text: SpatRaster one layer LS-factor values (dimensionless, values clamped 0 ), extent CRS (possibly reprojected) input DEM. layer named "LS_factor".

title: Calculate Topographic LS-Factor — calc_ls_factor
text: LS-factor calculated : $$LS = \left(\frac{}{22.13}\right)^{0.4} \cdot \left(\frac{\sin(\beta)}{0.0896}\right)^{1.3}$$ \(\) cell size metres \(\beta\) slope radians. DEM geographic CRS (degrees), automatically reprojected appropriate UTM zone computation.

title: Calculate Topographic LS-Factor — calc_ls_factor
text: Moore, .D., & Burch, G.J. (1986). Physical basis length-slope factor Universal Soil Loss Equation. Soil Science Society America Journal, 50(5), 1294-1298.

title: Calculate Topographic LS-Factor — calc_ls_factor
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   dem <- terra::rast("srtm.tif")   ls  <- calc_ls_factor(dem)    # Without plot   ls  <- calc_ls_factor(dem, plot = FALSE) } # }

title: Calculate Rainfall Erosivity (R-Factor) — calc_r_factor
text: Computes RUSLE R-factor using empirical formula appropriate climate zone study area. zone detected automatically coordinates via get_climate_zone(), can set manually.

title: Calculate Rainfall Erosivity (R-Factor) — calc_r_factor
code: calc_r_factor(   precip_raster,   lat = NULL,   lon = NULL,   climate_zone = NULL,   season_days = 243,   a = 0.171,   b = 1.212,   verbose = TRUE,   plot = TRUE )

title: Calculate Rainfall Erosivity (R-Factor) — calc_r_factor
text: precip_raster SpatRaster. Either 1 layer (cumulative seasonal precipitation mm) 12 layers (monthly, Jan Dec). required number layers depends climate zone. function throws informative error wrong count supplied. lat Numeric. Latitude study area (decimal degrees). Required automatic zone detection unless climate_zone set manually. lon Numeric. Longitude study area (decimal degrees). climate_zone Character NULL. Manual override climate zone. Valid values: "winter_rain_north", "winter_rain_south", "summer_monsoon", "hyperarid", "continental", "australian". NULL (default), zone detected lat/lon. season_days Numeric. Length precipitation season days. used winter_rain_north / winter_rain_south (Bonilla & Vidal). Default: 243 (Southern Hemisphere, Jan Aug). Northern Hemisphere: 182. Numeric. Coefficient Bonilla & Vidal (2011). used winter_rain_*. Default: 0.171. b Numeric. Coefficient b Bonilla & Vidal (2011). used winter_rain_*. Default: 1.212. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints detected zone, formula, parameters recommended data period console. Default: TRUE. plot Logical. TRUE, displays map R-factor computation. Default: TRUE.

title: Calculate Rainfall Erosivity (R-Factor) — calc_r_factor
text: SpatRaster one layer R-factor values. attribute attr(result, "r_factor_meta") contains list : zone, formula_name, params (list parameters used), season_recommendation.

title: Calculate Rainfall Erosivity (R-Factor) — calc_r_factor
text: Bonilla & Vidal (2011). Rainfall erosivity central Chile. Journal Hydrology, 410(1-2), 126-133. Arnoldus (1980). approximation rainfall factor USLE. : De Boodt & Gabriels (eds.), Assessment Erosion. Wiley, 127-132. Yu & Rosewell (1996). robust estimator R-factor USLE. Transactions ASAE, 39(2), 559-561.

title: Calculate Rainfall Erosivity (R-Factor) — calc_r_factor
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   precip <- terra::rast("chirps_jan_aug.tif")   r <- calc_r_factor(precip, lat = -33.0, lon = -71.0)    # Manual zone override (skips get_climate_zone())   r <- calc_r_factor(precip, climate_zone = "winter_rain_south",                      season_days = 243)    # Without plot   r <- calc_r_factor(precip, lat = -33.0, lon = -71.0, plot = FALSE) } # }

what: Get recommended data aggregation period for a climate zone — get_season_recommendation
title: Get recommended data aggregation period for a climate zone — get_season_recommendation
text: Returns recommended aggregation period precipitation (CHIRPS), NDVI, NDWI given climate zone. three input datasets must always cover period, corresponding rainy season respective climate zone.

title: Get recommended data aggregation period for a climate zone — get_season_recommendation
code: get_season_recommendation(zone)

title: Get recommended data aggregation period for a climate zone — get_season_recommendation
text: zone Character string. One five climate zone IDs: "winter_rain", "summer_monsoon", "hyperarid", "continental", "australian".

title: Get recommended data aggregation period for a climate zone — get_season_recommendation
text: named list following elements: zone Climate zone ID (character) label Human-readable period label, e.g. "January - August (243 days)" months Integer vector recommended months, e.g. c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8) months_label Comma-separated month abbreviations, e.g. "Jan, Feb, Mar, ..." season_days Number days recommended period (integer) note Additional guidance note (character, may empty)

title: Get recommended data aggregation period for a climate zone — get_season_recommendation
